claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model should be certified for launch because aggregate readiness passed, rehearsal showed no severity-one incidents, and a 7% staged rollout with rollback and monitoring provides enough governance cover despite an unresolved model-card disclosure weakness affecting the developer-support migration segment.
specific_concerns: The governing policy requires either exclusion of the affected use case from rollout or approved risk acceptance before launch; the available evidence shows neither condition is met.
The affected developer-support migration segment remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort because assignment is random by organization.
The risk-acceptance document is only a draft, has a blank approver line, and does not address the specific exposed developer-support migration segment.
Aggregate readiness, staged rollout percentage, rollback capability, and monitoring do not satisfy the disclosure-policy predicate when the affected segment remains exposed.
unsupported_claims: The claim that rollout controls and reversibility provide sufficient temporary governance cover for certification is not supported under the stated policy because the affected segment is still exposed and risk acceptance is not approved.

The claim that certification is supportable, even narrowly, overstates what the admissible evidence permits; the evidence supports launch readiness in general but not compliance with the unresolved disclosure requirement.
evidence_requests: Provide an approved risk-acceptance record that explicitly addresses the developer-support migration exposure and explains why launch exposure is acceptable.
Provide rollout-gating evidence showing the affected developer-support migration segment is excluded from the initial launch cohort.
Provide evidence that the model-card disclosure weakness for the named launch use case has been resolved before launch.
decision_criteria: If the affected use case is excluded from the rollout, rollout controls could count toward compliance.
If approved risk acceptance explicitly covers the exposed developer-support migration segment, certification could become supportable.
If the model-card limitation is resolved and properly disclosed for the named use case before launch, the policy obstacle would be removed.
Absent one of those conditions, certification remains noncompliant regardless of aggregate readiness or monitoring controls.
